title: APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards 2026
program_type: University merit scholarship (tuition-fee rebate) awarded on separate application at admission, administered by the university's Scholarships & Merit Awards Committee
funding_type: Partial tuition-fee rebate only (university-funded); no living allowance
administering_authority: Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation (APU) - Scholarships & Merit Awards Committee
implementing_agency: Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation (APU) - Scholarships & Merit Awards Committee (same body administers the award)
programme_action: APU Scholarships & Merit Awards for International Students - "International Merit Awards" track, assessed on 2026/2027 final results
description: APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards are fee awards offered by the Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation, a private university in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, to new international students across its Foundation, Diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. The awards take the form of tuition-fee rebates of 30%, 20% or 10% of course/tuition fees, set by the applicant's 2026/2027 final examination results (A-Levels, O-Levels/IGCSE, IB Diploma or IB MYP). The awards are granted on a first-come, first-served basis and are renewable each academic year provided the holder maintains a minimum CGPA of 2.50. The scheme is explicitly open to applicants of all countries and nationalities and is tenable only for study at APU's campus in Malaysia.

programme_structure.award_types_detail: Three fee-rebate tiers keyed to 2026/2027 final results: A-Levels AAA / AAB / ABB-AAC; O-Levels/IGCSE 8-9 As / 6-7 As / 4-5 As; IB Diploma 34+ / 30-33 / 26-29 points; IB MYP 48+ / 44-47 / 35-43 points. Applicants demonstrating sports excellence (Olympics, SEA Games, Youth Olympics, Asian Games, World Cups, Commonwealth Games) may be considered case by case.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Awards are granted on a yearly basis and are renewable on maintaining a minimum CGPA of 2.50 at the end of each academic year; failure to meet the academic requirement results in termination or suspension of the award.
programme_structure.intake: Online application submitted through the APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards form on the official page; applicants must meet minimum entry requirements with actual results. APU's 2026 undergraduate intake dates include 24 November 2026 (example published for the BSc (Hons) Information Technology programme).

status_note: The published application deadline for the 2026/2027 cycle is 31 October 2026, which is after the verification date of 2026-10-03, so the cycle is live at the time of research. Awards are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, so the practical window closes earlier once the annual allocation of awards is exhausted. Next cycle expected to be published on the same official page for the following intake; re-verify after 31 October 2026.
verification_type: Official provider page read directly on the awarding body's own domain (apu.edu.my), covering the award conditions, deadline, benefit tiers and renewal criteria, plus corroboration of programme duration and international admission procedure from other official APU pages.
verification_notes: SUBSTITUTION RECORD. The assigned target, the Perdana International Scholarship Programme (Ministry of Higher Education Malaysia, administered under the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme, MTCP), was verified as no longer offered at bachelor's level. Official evidence: (1) the MOHE Scholarship Division portal's international category (biasiswa.mohe.gov.my, 'Antarabangsa' section) lists only the Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) and the Malaysia-Islamic Development Bank Joint Scholarship (M-IsDB) - Perdana is absent; (2) the MOHE services 'Scholarships' page (mohe.gov.my/en/services?id=27&view=category) likewise lists only MIS and M-IsDB under 'Antarabangsa'; (3) MIS is postgraduate-only - the 'Guidelines for the Application of Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) 2026' states applicants must 'intend to pursue full-time postgraduate studies (Master's/PhD) in Malaysia' and lists only Master's degree and Doctor of Philosophy under Level of Study; (4) the MTCP Scholarship, the successor MTCP-administered scheme, is Master's-only - the MTCP Scholarship 2026 guidelines state 'This scholarship is open for full-time Master's Degree only for the September/October intake for the academic year of 2026/2027', and the official MTCP Scholarship 2026 FAQ answers 'Can I receive this scholarship for Undergraduate studies or PhD studies?' with 'No. This scholarship programme is only open for Master's degree studies.' The widely mirrored 2006-era Perdana figures (MYR 500 monthly maintenance, MYR 328 book allowance, not more than 21 years of age by 1 July 2006) could not be located on any current official Malaysian government page and are treated as obsolete and are not reproduced here. No official page was found announcing a formal cessation date for Perdana, so the discontinuation is established by absence from the current official programme lists plus the explicit postgraduate-only rules of both successor schemes, not by a dated closure notice. As directed, a live non-excluded Malaysia bachelor's scholarship was substituted into this same file slot.
source_last_updated: Not published as a discrete date; the APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards 2026 page carries the 2026/2027 results cycle and a 31 October 2026 deadline. The APU site footer states 'Copyright 2026 (c) Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation'.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: The award page publishes a single closing date of 31 October 2026 for the 2026/2027 cycle. APU advises applications 6-8 weeks in advance of the scheduled intake.
application_deadline.application_period: Open at time of research for the 2026/2027 intake, closing 31 October 2026; allocation is first come, first served, so the effective window can close earlier.
application_deadline.official_rule: "The deadline for this International Scholarship & Merit Awards is 31 October 2026. We must receive the full set of documents for scholarship application on or before this date. All Scholarships & Merit Awards are on first come first serve basis."
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Awards are first come, first served and APU reserves the right to decide the number of awards per programme, so practical availability can end before 31 October 2026. Documents must be received (not merely submitted) by the deadline; an incomplete application will not be considered.

programme_duration.official_range: Not published as a scholarship duration. APU's published bachelor's programme length is 3 years for the BSc (Hons) Information Technology programme used as reference; individual APU undergraduate programmes run 3 years or more.
programme_duration.renewal_note: The fee rebate itself is granted per academic year and renewed on maintaining a minimum CGPA of 2.50 at the end of each academic year. The underlying degree is not extendable by this award.

funding.scholarship_type: Partial tuition-fee rebate (discount) awarded on merit at admission
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend, maintenance allowance or living allowance is published. The award is expressed as a percentage rebate of course/tuition fees.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel or airfare support is published. Travel expenses are expressly listed among the costs borne by the award holder.
funding.institutional_costs: The award covers course/tuition fees only. Registration fees, accommodation fees, deposits, partner-university fees, resit or retake fees, and living and travel expenses are borne by the award holder.
funding.fully_funded_note: This is not a fully funded award. It is a partial tuition-fee rebate of at most 30% of course/tuition fees, with no living allowance, travel support, visa support or insurance, and it requires the applicant to pay a non-refundable RM 3,600 pre-arrival application and processing fee to accept the offer.

tuition.amount: 30%, 20% or 10% of course/tuition fees, depending on qualification tier
tuition.conditions: Percentage rebate on course/tuition fees only; secured by paying the RM 3,600 (approx. USD 950) pre-arrival application and processing fee; renewed annually on maintaining CGPA 2.50.

visa_support.note: Visa application costs are borne by the applicant; EMGS visa processing fees are charged to the applicant within the RM 3,600 pre-arrival fee.

insurance.note: Not covered by the award; APU publishes separate insurance information for international students as a student cost.

accommodation_support.note: Accommodation fees are expressly excluded from the award and borne by the award holder; the RM 3,600 pre-arrival fee covers accommodation on first arrival only.

bond.note: No service bond is published. APU instead requires repayment in full of the total value awarded if the recipient fails to comply with all terms and conditions of the award.

total_estimated_value.note: Deliberately not computed. The award is a percentage of course/tuition fees and APU does not publish an absolute value on the award page.

coverage: Partial tuition-fee rebate (30%, 20% or 10% tier) on course/tuition fees only
coverage_limitations: Registration fees, accommodation fees, deposits, partner-university fees, resit or retake fees, and living and travel expenses are expressly excluded and borne by the award holder.
No monthly stipend, living allowance, travel allowance, installation allowance, insurance or visa-cost support is provided.
Awards are not transferable or exchangeable for cash, in part or in full.
APU reserves the right to decide the number of awards to be awarded for each programme, so availability is not guaranteed at any tier.
Awards apply to study at APU in Malaysia only and are not applicable for study at overseas partner universities.
Exact benefit structure may differ by programme, qualification and intake year; the tier table published is keyed specifically to 2026/2027 final results and may be revised for later cycles.
eligible_applicants: New international students applying to APU
Applicants of all countries and nationalities
School leavers and applicants with A-Levels, O-Levels/IGCSE, IB Diploma or IB MYP results
Applicants awaiting final results, who may apply on forecast results and receive a conditional offer
Applicants with international sports excellence, considered case by case
final_year_condition: Final-year secondary / high-school students are eligible: APU states that undergraduate applicants 'may apply with your forecast results if you are still awaiting the final results; we will then make you a conditional offer on you achieving specified grades in your final exams'. The award tier itself is fixed to the final results actually achieved.
equivalent_degree_note: Equivalent international qualifications are accepted and each maps to an award tier: A-Levels, O-Levels/IGCSE, IB Diploma and IB MYP are each listed explicitly in the tier table. Other international qualifications ('Other International Qualifications') are accepted for admission and assessed by the Scholarships & Merit Awards Committee.

eligibility.citizenship: Open to all countries and nationalities; the award page states the scheme 'is applicable to all countries / nationalities'. It is the international-student track of APU's Merit Awards, distinct from the Malaysian-student track.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement is published. The award is tenable only for study at APU in Malaysia, and international students must be outside Malaysia while the student pass is processed.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Applicants must meet APU's minimum entry requirements with actual results (or forecast results leading to a conditional offer). Qualification-based tiers: A-Levels AAA / AAB / ABB-AAC; O-Levels/IGCSE 8-9 As / 6-7 As / 4-5 As; IB Diploma 34+ / 30-33 / 26-29; IB MYP 48+ / 44-47 / 35-43.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Final results at the published thresholds determine the rebate tier. Applicants must 'fulfil the Award Academic Entry Requirements with actual results'. Renewal requires maintaining a minimum CGPA of 2.50 at the end of each academic year.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: CGPA 2.50 minimum at APU, required to retain and renew the award in subsequent years. No minimum secondary-school CGPA is published; entry is measured by the qualification thresholds above.
eligibility.language_requirement: Evidence of English language proficiency (copies of IELTS/TOEFL etc.) is required as part of admission and as a scholarship application document. The award page does not publish a minimum band score; APU's official programme entry requirements set the exact score per programme.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Not required for the Merit Awards. International sports excellence (Olympics, SEA Games, Youth Olympics, Asian Games, World Cups, Commonwealth Games) may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
eligibility.financial_need: Not a criterion; the awards are merit-based on final examination results.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: No restriction on holding another award is published for the APU International Merit Awards. The scheme is limited to 'new international students'.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Applicants must be new international students enrolling at APU; existing students are covered by APU's returning-student route rather than this award.
eligibility.health_requirement: A signed Health Declaration Form is required, and a medical screening applies as part of the Malaysian student-pass process via EMGS.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None at award level. All APU Foundation, Diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate programmes are within scope, though APU sets the number of awards available per programme. Dual-degree study at overseas partner universities is excluded.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: APU does not publish a percentage or CGPA threshold for the initial award; the tier is determined by the qualification thresholds listed. The only published numeric academic threshold is the CGPA 2.50 minimum required for annual renewal.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: All applicants must meet APU's minimum entry requirements for the chosen programme. Entry requirements and English scores are programme-specific and published on APU's individual course pages rather than on the scholarship page.
selection_factors_may_include: Application submission date (first come, first served)
International sports excellence, case by case
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: The award is not a holistic or committee-scored competition; it is a published results-to-rebate mapping applied in order of application, subject to committee discretion on the number of awards per programme.

english_requirement.moi_rule: Not published on the award page. APU's international admission procedure requires 'Copies of IELTS/TOEFL etc to evaluate English Language Proficiency' and 'IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/MUET English Certification Results' at offer-acceptance stage.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The award page requires English proficiency evidence but does not publish any minimum score. Exact IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/MUET thresholds are set per programme in APU's official entry requirements and must be checked on the individual course page; no score is asserted here because none is traceable to the award page.

language_of_instruction.language_note: APU is an English-medium university in Kuala Lumpur; application documents are required in English or with certified English translation, and English proficiency evidence is required for admission. The award page does not separately state the language of instruction.

application_method.application_route: Direct online application by the student through the APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards form published on the official award page on apu.edu.my, alongside the APU online application for the chosen programme.
application_steps: Complete the APU online application form for the chosen programme and intake at admissions.apu.edu.my, indicating the programme and intake date.

Submit the 'APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards' online form on the official award page with nationality, contact details, programme of interest, current qualification and educational documents.
Attach up to ten relevant academic documents (jpg, gif, png, pdf, doc, docx, ppt, pptx, rar, zip; each file under 1 MB).
Secure the award by paying the RM 3,600 (approx. USD 950) pre-arrival application and processing fee to accept the offer.

Furnish passport copies (valid at least 24 months from the intake date), passport photographs, certified academic documents with English translations, Health Declaration Form and English test results for the EMGS student-pass process.
Receive the Visa Approval Letter (VAL) and travel to Malaysia for the intake.

application_fee.note: Pre-arrival Application Processing Fees of RM 3,600 (approx. USD 950) are required to accept the offer and secure the award, comprising EMGS visa processing fees (and applicable EMGS GST), APU/APIIT application and processing fees, airport assistance and transfer, and accommodation on first arrival. The fee is non-refundable once the offer has been accepted.

selection_process.selection_type: Automatic, results-based tier mapping on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to committee discretion on the number of awards per programme.
possible_stages: Eligibility check against APU minimum entry requirements
Award tier assignment based on 2026/2027 final results
Offer issue and acceptance via RM 3,600 pre-arrival payment
selection_process.weighting_note: No weighting formula is published. The published rule set is a direct mapping from final results to a rebate percentage, applied in order of application.
selection_process.results_timing: APU states applicants 'will normally receive the results in 2-3 working days upon receiving the complete documents' for the admission offer; no separate scholarship decision date is published. Award allocation continues until the 31 October 2026 deadline or until awards are exhausted.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Awards are tiered (30% / 20% / 10%) by qualification threshold rather than ranked or competitively scored.

Order of application, since awards are first come, first served

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: An APU bachelor's degree with honours (for example Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Information Technology), awarded by APU, Malaysia.
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 3 years full-time for the APU BSc (Hons) Information Technology programme used as reference; other APU undergraduate programmes may differ.
possible_awards: APU bachelor's degree with honours (awarding body: APU, Malaysia)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The reference APU BSc (Hons) Information Technology page states 'Duration 3 years', 'Full Time', 'Awarding Body APU, Malaysia'. Undergraduate programmes are delivered at APU's Kuala Lumpur campus; the award is not applicable for study at overseas partner universities.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: APU operates a credit transfer and exemption pathway (PaCE) and a Dual Degree Programme with De Montfort University; transfer students previously enrolled at another Malaysian institution must supply a visa cancellation and release letter and an attendance report of at least 80%.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Course/tuition fees are reduced by the awarded percentage (30%, 20% or 10%). All other fees remain payable by the student.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: Applicants must pay RM 3,600 (approx. USD 950) pre-arrival application and processing fee to accept the offer; this fee is non-refundable once the offer has been accepted.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Award holders must accept and comply with the published conditions of the awards, including academic progress, conduct, attendance and assignment requirements.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: APU provides an international student guide, student welcome team, campus residence, EMGS-linked student-pass and Visa Approval Letter processing, insurance information and a graduate pass pathway.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No service bond is published. Instead, 'Recipients who fail to comply with all the terms and conditions of the Awards will be required to pay back in full the total value awarded to him / her by APU.'
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Repayment in full of the total value awarded, plus termination or suspension of the award for failure to maintain the CGPA 2.50 requirement. International students who change programme must re-apply for a new student pass.

application_readiness_checklist: Hold or be about to receive final results at one of the published qualification thresholds (A-Levels, O-Levels/IGCSE, IB Diploma, IB MYP)
Passport valid for at least 24 months from the intended intake date
Certified academic documents available, with certified English translations where needed
An English proficiency test result available (IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/MUET)
RM 3,600 (approx. USD 950) available for the non-refundable pre-arrival application and processing fee
Complete the scholarship form early, because awards are first come, first served and limited per programme
programme_comparison_fields: Host institution and campus (APU, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia)
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No motivation letter, essay or personal statement is required for the International Merit Awards, so effort is better spent on achieving the qualification threshold that unlocks a higher tier and on submitting a complete document set early. APU accepts forecast results, so an applicant awaiting final results should apply on those and secure a conditional offer rather than waiting.
common_mistakes: Assuming the award is fully funded when it covers course/tuition fees only and excludes registration, accommodation, deposit, resit and living costs
Waiting until the 31 October 2026 deadline even though awards are first come, first served and capped per programme
Applying with predicted results without following up with the actual final results that determine the tier
Treating the RM 3,600 pre-arrival fee as refundable or as a fee covered by the scholarship
Uploading oversized or uncertified documents and having the application ignored as incomplete
Assuming the award follows the student to an overseas partner university under the dual-degree scheme
Assuming a minimum IELTS/TOEFL score is published on the award page when the threshold is programme-specific

risk_flags.risk: Award allocation is first come, first served and capped per programme
risk_flags.impact: A qualifying applicant may receive no award even before the 31 October 2026 deadline, or may receive a lower tier than another applicant with identical grades
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply as early as possible with a complete document set, and confirm current availability with scholarship@apu.edu.my before relying on the award in a funding plan

risk_flags.risk: The award is a partial tuition rebate with no living allowance
risk_flags.impact: Living costs, accommodation, registration fees, resit fees, travel and visa costs are unfunded and must be financed privately
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget the full cost of study in Kuala Lumpur independently; treat the rebate as a fee discount rather than scholarship income

risk_flags.risk: A non-refundable RM 3,600 pre-arrival fee is required to accept the offer and secure the award
risk_flags.impact: Applicants pay a significant sum that is not recoverable if they later withdraw
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the fee conditions and the refund policy before accepting; confirm the programme and intake decision first

risk_flags.risk: Annual renewal depends on maintaining CGPA 2.50
risk_flags.impact: The rebate is lost or suspended in later years if academic performance falls below the threshold
risk_flags.mitigation: Maintain the CGPA requirement and obtain the official APU entry requirements early to plan coursework

risk_flags.risk: The qualification-tier table is specific to 2026/2027 final results
risk_flags.impact: Tiers and thresholds may be revised for the next cycle, so the published values are not guaranteed to persist
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-verify the tier table on the official page before applying for a later cycle; next verification due 2026-11-01

risk_flags.risk: The scheme is administered by a single private university, not a national government
risk_flags.impact: No Malaysian government-funded international bachelor's scholarship is currently verified as live; the award carries no government standing and covers only one institution
risk_flags.mitigation: Do not rely on a Malaysian government undergraduate international scholarship; check individual universities separately

risk_flags.risk: Changing programme requires a new student pass
risk_flags.impact: International students who switch programme must re-apply for a student pass, adding cost and time, and may jeopardise the award
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm the intended programme before accepting the offer; the award is programme-specific

risk_flags.risk: This record is a substitution for a discontinued target
risk_flags.impact: Readers searching for the Perdana International Scholarship Programme will land on an unrelated university award
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the substitution note in verification_notes and database_notes; Perdana is discontinued at bachelor's level and its MTCP successor is Master's-only

Submit APU International Students Scholarships & Merit Awards form with documents
Accept offer and pay RM 3,600 pre-arrival application and processing fee

best_fit: An international school leaver of any nationality holding (or expecting) strong A-Level, IGCSE or IB results who wants to study a bachelor's degree at APU in Kuala Lumpur, can fund their own living costs and accommodation, and wants a partial tuition-fee reduction rather than a fully funded award.
not_best_fit: Applicants seeking a fully funded scholarship with a living stipend, airfare, insurance or visa-cost support
Applicants who cannot fund living costs, accommodation and registration fees themselves
Applicants who want a Malaysian government-sponsored international bachelor's scholarship; the Perdana scheme is discontinued and its MTCP and MIS successors are Master's-only
Applicants who want to study at a Malaysian public university, or to transfer to an overseas partner university under a dual-degree scheme
Applicants without A-Level, IGCSE, IB Diploma or IB MYP results, since these are the only published qualification tiers
Late applicants, since awards are first come, first served and can be exhausted before 31 October 2026

database_notes: SUBSTITUTION: This file was assigned to the Perdana International Scholarship Programme (Ministry of Higher Education Malaysia, administered under the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme), a bachelor's-level international scholarship. That programme is discontinued at bachelor's level, so this record is a live substitute Malaysia bachelor's scholarship in the same filename slot.

PERDANA STATUS - NOT LIVE FOR BACHELOR'S LEVEL. Evidence: (a) the MOHE Scholarship Division portal (biasiswa.mohe.gov.my) lists, under its 'Antarabangsa' (International) category, only the Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) and the Malaysia-Islamic Development Bank Joint Scholarship (M-IsDB) - Perdana does not appear; (b) the MOHE services 'Scholarships' page (mohe.gov.my) repeats the same two-programme list; (c) MIS is postgraduate-only, per its own 2026 guidelines ('intend to pursue full-time postgraduate studies (Master's/PhD) in Malaysia'; Level of Study lists only Master's degree and Doctor of Philosophy); (d) the MTCP Scholarship, the MTCP-administered successor to Perdana, is explicitly 'open for full-time Master's Degree only' for 2026/2027, and its official FAQ answers 'Can I receive this scholarship for Undergraduate studies or PhD studies?' with 'No. This scholarship programme is only open for Master's degree studies.'

Perdana's current participating-country list could not be established because the scheme is no longer advertised. The current participating-country list for the MTCP successor is the 144-country list published at mtcp.kln.gov.my ('List of Countries Eligible to Apply for the MTCP Scholarship'), recorded in verification.source_citations; this is not a Perdana benefit.

The 2006-era Perdana benefit figures widely mirrored on third-party sites (MYR 500 per month maintenance, MYR 328 book allowance, 'not more than 21 years of age by 1 July 2006') were not found on any current official Malaysian government domain and are deliberately not recorded as this scheme's benefits. They are recorded here only as removed, unverified legacy claims.

Current successor benefit structure, recorded for reference only: the MTCP Scholarship 2026 covers tuition fees paid directly to the university, a monthly allowance paid into a Malaysian bank account, and one economy-class return airfare; age limit 45; IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 60 or a degree taught in English; minimum Second Class Upper (Honours) / CGPA 3.00 at undergraduate level; application window 4 May - 12 June 2026. It is Master's-only and is therefore not a valid bachelor's substitute, which is why a university award was substituted instead.

No official page announcing a formal cessation date for Perdana was located. The discontinuation is therefore established by absence from both current official MOHE programme lists combined with the explicit postgraduate-only scope of both successor schemes, rather than by a dated closure notice.
SHORT_TITLE: 'APU International Merit Awards' is a descriptive short form; APU does not publish an acronym for this award.
LEGACY_TITLES: none found; no earlier or alternative name for this award is published.

No minimum IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/MUET score is published on the award page, so all english_requirement minimum scores are null. The thresholds are programme-specific and published on individual APU course pages.

No absolute award value in MYR is published; the award is expressed only as a percentage rebate. No total estimated value has been computed, per the contract's prohibition on presenting a computed total as an award.

Programme duration of 3 years is taken from the APU BSc (Hons) Information Technology page as the reference undergraduate programme; APU publishes programme length per course rather than a single scholarship-wide duration.

The logo is the primary navbar logo served from the awarding body's own domain and rendered on the official APU pages used for this record. The domain favicon returns HTTP 404, so the navbar logo was used. No photograph was taken from an official source, so image_url is null.
